_note: Curated HSN value chains of the India Manufacturing Atlas. Every chain is curated from real GST-master / HS 2022 codes and public industry structure. Ministry ownership is taken from the Atlas's own product mapping (products.ministry_id / product_ministries) so the chain pages and product pages never disagree. Items carry an HS code (2/4/6/8 digits), a description and an item name. Edges connect an input to the next stage's item (relation input_to).
_schema: chains[]{id, name, title, anchor_hs, lead_ministry_id, description, phase, source, sort_order, stages[]{id, name, order, ministry_text, ministry_ids, items[]{item, hs_code, description, ministry_text, ministry_ids, source}}, edges[]{src, dst, relation, source?}, manufacturers[]{name, url}, clusters[]{id, name, state, district, products, lat, lon, sector_ids?}, skill_council{...}}

chains.name: Tyre
chains.title: Tyre Sector (HS Code 4011)

chains.name: Natural Rubber
chains.title: Natural Rubber Sector (HS Code 4001)
chains.description: Natural rubber is tapped as latex from the rubber tree (Hevea brasiliensis) and processed into latex concentrate, ribbed smoked sheets, crepes and technically specified rubber (TSNR). It is the principal raw material of tyres and of conveyor belts, hoses, seals, gaskets, gloves and footwear. India is a large producer but a net importer of natural rubber; the Rubber Board under the Department of Commerce oversees the sector.

chains.name: Cotton Textiles & Apparel
chains.title: Cotton Textiles & Apparel Sector (HS Chapter 52)
chains.description: India's cotton value chain runs from raw cotton through ginning, spinning, knitting or weaving and dyeing to finished garments. It is one of the country's largest manufacturing employers, organised in clusters such as Tiruppur (knitwear), Ludhiana (hosiery) and Coimbatore (spinning). Cotton T-shirts (6109 10 00) and women's cotton dresses (6204 42 90) sit at the end of this chain.

chains.name: Pharmaceuticals (KSM to Formulations)
chains.title: Pharmaceutical Formulations Sector (HS Code 3004)
chains.description: Medicines move from key starting materials (KSMs) and intermediates to active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and then to finished formulations. chains.name: Iron & Steel
chains.title: Iron & Steel Sector (HS Chapter 72)
chains.description: Integrated plants smelt iron ore with coking coal and limestone into hot metal, while coal-based direct reduction yields sponge iron; both feed steel melting shops that cast ingots, billets and slabs. These are rolled into flat products (hot-rolled, cold-rolled and coated coil) and long products (bars and wire rod) and further into pipes and tubes. India is the world's second-largest crude steel producer.

chains.name: Sports Goods
chains.title: Sports Goods (HS Code 9506)
chains.description: Sports goods under heading 9506 are made in MSME clusters - Jalandhar and Meerut above all - from natural and synthetic rubber, PU and PVC coated fabric, leather, willow, cork and feathers. India is a net exporter of inflatable and other balls (9506.62, 9506.69) and of outdoor-game equipment (9506.99), but imports most gym, fitness and athletics equipment (9506.91), golf and skates.

chains.name: Bicycles
chains.title: Bicycles (HS Code 8712)
chains.description: Non-motorised bicycles are assembled from steel or aluminium tube frames, rims, spokes, hubs, free-wheels, chains, brakes, saddles, pedals and crank sets, rolling on rubber tyres and tubes. Ludhiana is the centre of India's bicycle and cycle-parts industry, supplied by its fastener, metal-parts and steel re-rolling units.

chains.name: Sporting Firearms
chains.title: Sporting & Air Guns (HS Codes 9303, 9304)
chains.description: Sporting shotguns and rifles are machined from forged alloy-steel bars (barrels, actions) and fitted with hardwood stocks; air guns use similar barrels with spring or gas mechanisms. Manufacture, sale, import and export need a licence under the Arms Act, 1959 and Arms Rules, 2016. Munger in Bihar is the registered gun cluster.
